headline: Anthropic Says Claude 5 Models Need Less Rigid Prompting, More Judgment
what_happened: Anthropic published new guidance on 'context engineering' for its Claude 5-generation models, arguing that newer models handle ambiguity well enough that developers should favor judgment-based guidance over rigid rules. As one proof point, Anthropic says it removed more than 80% of Claude Code's system prompt with no performance loss. The post recommends progressive disclosure -- loading detailed guidance into skills Claude invokes selectively -- and leaner CLAUDE.md files focused on repository-specific gotchas.
why_it_matters: This signals Anthropic sees Claude 5-generation models as reliable enough to need less hand-holding, shifting 'context engineering' -- curating what a model sees, not just what it's asked -- away from exhaustive rulebooks and toward concise, judgment-friendly instructions, reshaping how agentic coding tools get built.
one_liner: Anthropic is telling developers that Claude's newest models are smart enough to follow loose guidance instead of long lists of rigid rules.

citations.quote: Newer models have better judgement and can handle these decisions well without explicit rules.
